home.headline: You get four votes. Three in four Bramptonians used none.
home.standfirst: A plain-language guide to who is running, what the City actually does with $1.38 billion a year, and what the next four years decide. Built on Brampton's own open data, with every number traced to its source.
home.advanceNote: Advance voting opens in {days} days — 9, 10, 11, 16 and 17 October.
home.advanceOpenNote: Advance voting is open now — any location, any ward.
home.ballotTitle: Your ballot has four questions on it
home.ballotSub: Most people only know about the first one.
home.pairNote: Questions 2 and 3 are decided by your ward pair, not your ward alone.
home.turnoutTitle: Fewer than one in four eligible Bramptonians voted last time.
home.turnoutBody: The Ontario municipal average was 32.9%. A city councillor here can win a seat representing roughly 130,000 residents on a few thousand votes — which is why the four people on your ballot are the easiest politicians in Canada to influence, and the hardest to find information about.
home.addressHelp: Returns your ward, your ward pair, the races you vote in and where to vote. The lookup runs in your browser — your address is never sent anywhere.
home.fieldNote: {n} certified candidates are contesting the 11 seats on city council.

basics.title: Brampton 101
basics.standfirst: Brampton is governed by two councils at once, and almost nobody can name which one handles their complaint. This page is the map: who is elected, by whom, how often, and which government to phone.
basics.boundaryNote: Ward boundaries were reviewed and the review was paused pending provincial decisions on Peel. The 2026 election uses the same boundaries as 2022.
basics.wardsTitle: The ten wards, and the five pairs
basics.holdsNow: Who holds each pair right now
basics.pairsIntro: Every ward is paired with one other ward. The pair elects two people: a Regional Councillor and a City Councillor. Both represent you; only one of them also sits at Peel Region.
basics.whyPairsBody: It keeps council small — 11 people for a city of 656,480 — while giving each area two voices. The trade-off is that a single councillor answers to roughly 130,000 residents.
basics.cityCouncilBody: The mayor, five Regional Councillors and five City Councillors. Every one of the eleven is elected directly by you — the mayor city-wide, the other ten by ward pair.
basics.strongMayor: The mayor holds strong-mayor powers: they can propose the budget, which council needs a two-thirds vote to amend, and can veto bylaws touching provincial priorities.
basics.peelCouncilBody: Chair plus 24 members shared between three municipalities: Mississauga 12, Brampton 9, Caledon 3.
basics.peelCouncilNote: Brampton's nine are the mayor, the five Regional Councillors you elect, and three City Councillors that council picks itself after the election — the one seat on your ballot you do not actually choose.
basics.whoToPhoneSub: The single most useful thing on this site.

money.title: Where the money goes
money.kicker: Running page · rechecked until election day
money.standfirst: Brampton will spend about $1.38 billion this year. This page tracks what that buys, who says it is working, and who says it is not — with the name of whoever made each claim attached to it.
money.chartNote: Every chart carries its source underneath it. No exceptions.
money.goodBad: What is good, what is bad
money.goodBadIntro: We do not score the budget ourselves. We collect the strongest published case on each side and name who made it, so you can weigh them yourself.
money.caseFor: The case that it is working
money.caseAgainst: The case that it is not
money.method: Figures are taken from the City's published budget documents. Criticism is quoted and attributed, never paraphrased into our own voice. Anything we cannot trace to a primary document is marked as not yet sourced.

issues.title: The problems
issues.kicker: Running page · six issues, tracked to election day
issues.standfirst: Each issue gets the same treatment: the measurable evidence, whose job it actually is, and then every candidate's position — quoted from something they published, or marked as missing. We never guess what a candidate thinks.
issues.positionsSourced: {done}/{total} candidates for council have a sourced position on this
issues.statusBody: candidate-issue positions sourced. {n} candidates for council across {i} issues. This counter is the honest measure of how finished this site is.
issues.howTitle: How a position gets onto this site
issues.how1: We find it published — a campaign site, a filed platform, a recorded all-candidates meeting, a news interview.
issues.how2: We quote it verbatim and link the original. No paraphrase, no summary in our voice.
issues.how3: We email the candidate the page and offer a correction before and after it goes live.
issues.how4: If nothing exists, the slot stays visibly empty. An empty slot is information too.

candidates.title: Election 2026
candidates.standfirst: Nominations closed on 21 August. Every name below is from the City Clerk's certified list — the field cannot change now. What can change is how much we know about each of them.
candidates.ballotOrder: Sorted as the ballot will be: alphabetical by surname.
candidates.racesSub: You vote in exactly one of these five rows.
candidates.alsoBallotBody: a school trustee. Peel District, Dufferin-Peel Catholic, Conseil scolaire Viamonde or Conseil scolaire catholique MonAvenir, depending on how you are registered.
candidates.courtNote: Certified 25 August 2026 by order of the Ontario Superior Court.
candidates.acclaimedNote: Acclaimed — no opponent. This seat is already decided.
candidates.rightOfReply: Right of reply is open. Corrections are logged publicly with a date.
candidates.standTitle: Where they stand, issue by issue
candidates.standIntro: Two kinds of entry only. A verified record is something this person actually did or voted for, traceable to a council document. Everything else stays marked not yet sourced until they publish a position we can quote.
candidates.moneyBody: Nothing to show yet, and that is not an oversight. Candidates file financial statements after election day. When the filings land we will publish contributor totals for every candidate on the same page, side by side.
candidates.wontBody: No endorsements. No scores or grades. No inferring a position from party history, a donor list or a past job. If we cannot quote it, it is not on the page.
candidates.areYouBody: Send us your platform and we will quote it in full within 48 hours, before election day. Corrections take priority over everything else we are building.
